summary: No control area or Article 4 direction for holiday lets. A 2018 council report said most short lets in Bath (3 or fewer rooms) stay in the C3 home use class; larger ones can be a material change of use.
No control area or Article 4 direction for holiday lets; city-wide Article 4 covers HMOs only. Whole-home short lets are decided case by case under the Birmingham Development Plan (adopted 2017).

The council says most Airbnb-style holiday lets need planning permission: self-contained holiday flats and houses with no on-site management are a sui generis use. Outside the Town Centre, Resort Core and 6 Holiday Accommodation Areas, permission "generally will not be granted".

A 2026 Full Council motion asks officers to investigate whether homes let for more than 90 nights a year are a material change of use and to gather evidence for a possible Article 4 direction. Nothing decided.
The council says you might need permission depending on how much the use changes. Zones where short lets are allowed or restricted are being looked at for City Plan 2041; nothing new applies yet.
Draft Local Plan 2022-2040 Policy H2 would refuse the loss of an existing home, with narrow exceptions; adoption expected late 2026. Whether the main modifications change H2: UNVERIFIED.

Local Plan 2018 Policy 3 allows changing housing to other uses only in exceptional circumstances; in Jan 2018 officers recommended enforcement notices against 13 flats used as short-term visitor accommodation. Draft Greater Cambridge Local Plan Policy J/VA would go further (not in force).

No short-let control area or Article 4 direction for holiday lets found. England has no short-let use class, so the council decides case by case whether letting a whole home is a material change of use.

In West Wittering parish, Neighbourhood Plan Policy WW5 (made 28 Nov 2023) only supports new open-market homes limited to use as a principal residence. Elsewhere, decided case by case; no district-wide holiday-let policy found.

Submission Draft Local Plan 2043 Policy TC7 would only support new short-term lets where fewer than 10% of properties within 100 m are HMOs and there is no over-concentration of short lets, with a management plan. Not examined or adopted.

SWDPR Policy SWDPR 45 permits visitor accommodation (including self-catering) in Development Boundaries and limits countryside sites to set cases. No holiday-let Article 4. Malvern Hills National Landscape is not a National Park planning authority.

No control area or Article 4 direction for holiday lets. A 2024 council report says planning law does not currently require a change of use for a home to be used as a short-term let; the new Local Plan has no short-let policy.

Local Plan Policy DM22 supports tourism and leisure within or next to settlements; countryside sites need justification. No holiday-let Article 4. A small part of the district is in Dartmoor National Park.
The National Park Authority's draft Local Plan (Aug 2026) proposes a principal residence condition on all net new open-market homes in the Park. Not adopted; would not apply to existing homes.

Joint Local Plan Policy PLY21 supports visitor accommodation (including self-catering) in the core tourism area and resists losing important visitor facilities. No holiday-let Article 4; HMO Article 4 only.
Portsmouth Plan (adopted 2012) supports tourist-related facilities including hotels linked to the waterfront and maritime heritage. No holiday-let Article 4 (planning.data lists none).

Core Strategy Key Statement EC3 and Policy DMB3 support visitor accommodation and tourism facilities; extra design tests in the Forest of Bowland National Landscape. No holiday-let Article 4. Ribble Valley Borough Council remains the planning authority.

Proposed Submission Local Plan 2025-2042 (consultation 12 Oct to 24 Nov 2026): principal-residence-only for some new countryside homes, and proposals that lose homes to holiday accommodation not supported in Camber, Rye, Rye Foreign and Icklesham. Not in force.

Short Term Holiday Lets SPD (adopted 5 Dec 2024): a home let whole to one family-sized group is unlikely to need permission, but letting rooms separately, adding bedrooms or larger groups is likely to. In Primarily Residential Areas a conversion is refused if 5% of properties within 100 m are already short lets, flats or HMOs.

SAMDev Policy MD11 resists new holiday lets in the countryside unless a caravan or a conversion of a suitable rural building, and conditions new visitor accommodation against residential use. No holiday-let Article 4.
